Deployability of biotechnologies for environmentally resilient agriculture.
articles.abstract: NA: Agriculture is both humanity's largest infrastructure and the leading driver of environmental degradation. Many early-stage biotechnologies could mitigate this impact, but their deployability has not been systematically evaluated. We analyze deployability of 77 biotechnologies across eight domains (crops, soils, livestock, watersheds, aquaculture, health and security, food loss/waste and frontiers) by applying a Balanced Readiness Level assessment spanning technological, market, regulatory, acceptance and organizational dimensions. We find that market viability and social acceptance, not technological readiness, represent the primary constraints. High-readiness technologies tend to be 'drop-in', contained, transient and perceived as natural. These characteristics indicate strategies to elevate overall deployability, such as addressing genetically modified organism containment. Assessing the scalability and environmental impacts of biotechnologies for prioritization requires additional quantitative analysis, as shown in a Fermi analysis of microbial fertilizers. We combine our findings into a near- to long-term roadmap for living infrastructure: predictively designed multicomponent biological communities that function as systems at the ecosystem level to enhance food security and environmental resilience.

articles.title: Lasting genetic control of mosquito-borne diseases is within reach.
Cellular agriculture for sustainable and programmable foods.
articles.abstract: NA: Cellular agriculture promises to reduce the environmental burden and inefficiencies of food systems. The question is no longer whether precision fermentation and cultivated meat production can produce alternative proteins and other food components, but whether they can attain the cost, scale and quality required for broad adoption. We examine cellular agriculture through the interrelated lenses of enabling technologies, food function and manufacturing economics. The field is approaching an inflection point where biological technology development is less important for commercial success than achieving scalable, affordable manufacturing. Key challenges include how products and their functional attributes are designed and how production processes are configured. For precision fermentation, the most compelling opportunities lie in functional approaches to improve taste, nutritional quality, health benefits and formulation rather than in direct imitation of existing foods or ingredients. For cultivated meat production, impact will come first from hybrid and ingredient-based products that capture specific values of cellular ingredients while avoiding the costs of full tissue mimicry.

Cas12a-based combinatorial knockout screens define the genetic architecture of the DNA damage response.
articles.abstract: NA: To elucidate the genetic architecture of the DNA damage response (DDR) network, we conduct unbiased genetic interaction screens using Cas12a. We disrupt 233 DDR genes frequently mutated in cancer and other genetic diseases, either individually or in pairwise combinations, enabling us to assess the phenotypic effects induced by the loss of DDR gene pairs under unperturbed cell growth conditions. We identify high-confidence positive and negative gene-gene interactions, along with connections between previously unlinked DDR pathways. Among the identified genetic interactions, we uncover synthetic lethal interactions between genes encoding the translesion polymerase REV1-Pol ζ complex and the MCM8-MCM9-HROB DNA helicase complex, between Fanconi anemia genes and various mitotic DNA repair genes, as well as between genes encoding the DNA translocase SMARCAL1 and components of the FANCM complex, suggesting opportunities for targeted treatments in tumors carrying mutations in these genes. Collectively, our genetic map of the DDR network identifies synthetic lethal and buffering interactions with therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Editor's Pick: Wild Bioscience.
An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection.
articles.abstract: NA: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. The main site of H5N1 viral replication is the mammary tissue rather than the respiratory tract and viral transmission between animals is thought to occur through viral shedding in milk. Here, we generate an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine encoding the hemagglutinin (HA) of A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002/2024, representative of circulating bovine H5N1 viruses, and assess its immunogenicity and efficacy in lactating dairy cows. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis.

articles.title: An engineered, compact Cas12m variant for multiplexed gene activation in vivo.
articles.abstract: NA: Achieving coordinated CRISPR-based transactivation (CRISPRa) regulation in vivo remains challenging, as the requisite genetic elements frequently exceed the packaging capacity of AAV vectors. Here we report the identification and engineering of the Cas12m protein family, a naturally nuclease-dead CRISPR system that possesses intrinsic self-processing activity for its precursor crRNA. We develop an optimized variant, denCas12m, and leverage it in the smCRISPRa platform. We show that a single transcriptional unit encoding a multi-gRNA array can be processed into individual functional guides within a target cell, enabling efficient synergistic activation of a single gene through multiple sites or simultaneous activation of distinct endogenous genes from a single all-in-one AAV vector. We demonstrate phenotypic rescue in mouse models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and Scn1a haploinsufficiency. Furthermore, a single all-in-one AAV vector supports the simultaneous activation of multiple distinct endogenous genes in mice, with a single vector delivering up to eight crRNAs for activation of six different genes, demonstrating the platform's high-order multiplexing.

Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells.
articles.abstract: NA: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the 'recordanelle', a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

articles.title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells.
articles.abstract: NA: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf. In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet;CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

articles.title: Genetic code expansion enables plant-directed control of bacterial activity.
articles.abstract: NA: Microorganisms have the potential to deliver growth-promoting benefits to plants and crops; however, to be useful in a field setting, their gene expression should be programmable and restricted to specific plant hosts and conditions. Here, using O-methyl-L-tyrosine (OMY) as a model compound, we establish noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) as a tool for plant-based control of associated microbial activity. We use genetic code expansion to engineer OMY-dependent control of protein synthesis in the soil bacterium Bacillus subtilis. Engineered B. subtilis strains express an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase and tRNA pair that, upon provision of OMY, results in suppression of in-frame amber stop codons in target transcripts. We engineer Arabidopsis, tomato and poplar to biosynthesize OMY, showing that plant-derived OMY can stimulate gene expression in both model and wild soil bacteria. This demonstrates that inducible and tissue-specific expression of a single biosynthetic enzyme by the plant enables on-demand control over microbial activity, establishing ncAAs as a tool for programming plant-microorganism partnerships.

articles.title: Engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing.
articles.abstract: NA: Tools for manipulating RNA that rely on nonhuman proteins, such as ISC-based and Cas-based scaffolds, can lead to unintended and little-understood effects on human cells and present challenges in therapeutic translation. Replacing them with human proteins engineered for expanded, programmable functions could bypass the limitations of these foreign proteins. Here we demonstrate that human Argonaute 2 (AGO2) can be repurposed as a modular RNA targeting domain. AGO2 fused to a C-to-U deaminase enables AGO-led targeted editing of RNA (ALTER). Using guide RNAs that remodel target RNA structure for selective editing and reduced nuclease activity, we show that ALTER achieves, on average, 1.9-fold higher C-to-U editing on mRNA targets in HEK293T cells compared with Cas13 editors CURE and RESCUE. Transcriptome-wide RNA-seq revealed similar or lower levels of off-target editing compared to the same Cas13-based editors. Machine learning models predict that far fewer immunogenic peptides will result from ALTER and we show that ALTER is amenable to a validated workflow for artificial intelligence-directed deimmunization.
